note: Build three before applying: p3, p1 and p5 or p7. The rest are stretch projects for after week 6.

projects.name: Citations-first document Q&A with a measured retrieval pipeline
projects.pitch: Ask questions over a real public corpus and get answers where every claim links to a verified source passage.
projects.why_it_stands_out: Most candidates show a chatbot demo. You show a golden set, an ablation table and a citation verifier, which is what teams actually need.
corpus_ideas: Documentation of a framework you use (FastAPI, Django, Kubernetes)
A set of 200 arXiv papers on one topic
A government or university public FAQ and policy set
mvp: Ingest HTML or PDF into clean text with headings and source URLs as metadata
Heading-aware recursive chunking with overlap
Embeddings plus BM25 stored in Postgres (pgvector and full-text search)
Hybrid retrieval with Reciprocal Rank Fusion, then a cross-encoder reranker
Answer JSON with claims and citation ids; refuse when the context does not support an answer
Citation verifier: each cited quote must appear in the cited chunk
key_decisions: Chunk size and overlap, chosen from your own measurements
Hybrid weights or RRF constant
Reranker depth versus added latency
Abstention threshold and what the user sees when it triggers
evaluation: Golden set: 100 questions, 20 unanswerable, each with source passage ids
Retrieval: recall@5, recall@10, MRR
Generation: faithfulness (citation check plus judge), answer correctness
System: p50 and p95 latency, cost per query
One row per improvement in a before and after table
failure_modes_to_show: Stale content after a document update
Confident answer on an unanswerable question
stack: A sentence-embedding model and a reranker
pytest and a make eval target
deliverables: Public repo with a README that opens with the headline metric
One write-up: what moved recall@5 and what did not
talking_points: I built the golden set first so every change had a number.
Hybrid search plus reranking lifted recall@5 from X to Y at a cost of Z ms.
The citation verifier caught N fabricated quotes that a judge alone missed.

projects.name: Permission-aware enterprise search with leakage tests
projects.pitch: Multi-tenant search and Q&A where a user can never retrieve or be answered from documents they may not see.
projects.why_it_stands_out: It combines your full-stack strengths (auth, data modeling) with the security question interviewers love, and it has a pass or fail test suite.
corpus_ideas: Three fake tenants with generated documents in groups such as HR, Engineering and Finance
A public dataset split by department
mvp: Users, groups and per-document ACLs stored in Postgres
ACL metadata stored with every chunk; filtering applied before retrieval, never after
Query gateway that resolves the user's groups from a signed token
Cache keys that include tenant and permission hash
Audit log of who retrieved what
Leakage test suite with 30 attacks, including injection text hidden inside documents
key_decisions: Pre-filter versus post-filter and the recall impact
How fast an ACL change must take effect and how you propagate it
Why semantic caching across users is dangerous
evaluation: Leakage: zero leaked chunks across the attack suite
Recall@5 with filters on versus off
Time for an ACL change to take effect
Cost and latency overhead of filtering
failure_modes_to_show: Shared cache returns another tenant's answer
A document with hidden instructions asks the model to reveal other documents
stack: FastAPI, Postgres with pgvector or Qdrant payload filters
deliverables: Short write-up on pre-filter versus post-filter
talking_points: I treated ACLs as data in the index, not a UI concern.
My CI fails if any attack retrieves a forbidden chunk.

projects.name: Structured extraction service with cost-aware routing
projects.pitch: Turn invoices, resumes or contracts into validated JSON, using a cheap model first and a stronger model only when needed.
projects.why_it_stands_out: It shows reliability engineering: schemas, retries, confidence routing, a review queue and a cost per document number.
corpus_ideas: Synthetic resumes generated with known ground truth
Public contracts such as sample NDAs
mvp: Pydantic schema per document type
Validation with one retry that includes the error text
Routing: small model first, escalate on invalid output or low confidence
Async batch endpoint with idempotency keys
Human review queue page for escalated or invalid items
Field-level evaluation against 100 labeled documents
key_decisions: Which signal triggers escalation (schema failure, self-reported confidence, disagreement between two samples)
Per-field versus per-document accuracy
Where to redact personal data
evaluation: Field-level precision and recall
Escalation rate
Cost per document and per correct document
p95 latency for a batch of 100
failure_modes_to_show: Totals that do not equal the sum of line items
deliverables: Repo with sample documents and ground truth
Table of cost versus accuracy per routing strategy
talking_points: Routing cut cost by X percent with Y points of accuracy lost.
Validation errors are fed back, which fixed Z percent of failures on retry.

projects.name: Text-to-SQL analyst with schema retrieval and safe execution
projects.pitch: Ask a business question, get SQL, a result table and a chart, with guardrails that make it safe to connect to real data.
projects.why_it_stands_out: It joins retrieval, agents, security and evaluation in one project and has a crisp metric (execution accuracy).
corpus_ideas: A sanitized schema from an app you built
A public analytics dataset loaded into SQLite or Postgres
mvp: Index table and column descriptions and example queries; retrieve the relevant ones per question
Generate SQL, then validate by parsing (read-only, allowed tables only, automatic LIMIT)
Execute in a read-only role with a timeout
Repair loop with the database error, at most 2 attempts
Summarize the result and draw a chart
Eval of 60 question and SQL pairs scored by comparing result sets
key_decisions: How much schema to show the model per question
Whether to compare result sets or SQL text when scoring
How to handle ambiguous questions (ask or assume)
evaluation: Execution accuracy
Valid SQL rate
Repair success rate
Blocked unsafe queries in a test set of 20 attempts
Latency and cost per question
failure_modes_to_show: Prompt injection through a text column
deliverables: Failure analysis of the 10 worst questions
talking_points: Execution accuracy rose from X to Y after retrieving column descriptions.
No generated query can write because of the role and the parser.

projects.name: Research agent with a trace viewer and trajectory evals
projects.pitch: An orchestrator splits a research question across parallel workers, enforces cost caps, and writes a cited report you can inspect step by step.
projects.why_it_stands_out: You can show a single-agent versus multi-agent comparison with numbers and a failure taxonomy, plus a trace viewer you built yourself.
corpus_ideas: A fixed offline set of 200 documents so results are reproducible
mvp: Orchestrator that plans sub-questions
Parallel worker agents with search and read tools
Step, token and cost caps per run
Report with citations
Trace viewer page: timeline of calls with prompts, tools, tokens and cost
30-task eval with a rubric and success rate, steps and cost per task
key_decisions: How workers share context without copying everything
When to stop researching
What the orchestrator verifies versus trusts
evaluation: Task success rate
Average steps and tokens per task
Cost per task
Citation accuracy
Single-agent baseline comparison
stack: Provider tool-calling API or an agent SDK
Langfuse or your own trace store
A small React or plain HTML viewer
deliverables: Demo of one trace explained step by step
talking_points: Multi-agent improved success on broad questions by X but cost Y times more.
The trace viewer made failure analysis take minutes, not hours.
extensions: Self-critique pass before the final report

projects.name: LLM gateway with routing, caching, quotas and cost attribution
projects.pitch: An internal platform that sits in front of model providers and gives every team keys, budgets, fallbacks and a cost dashboard.
projects.why_it_stands_out: It plays to a backend developer's strengths and mirrors real platform teams: rate limiting, caching, failover and observability.
corpus_ideas: Replay a synthetic traffic file of 10,000 requests
mvp: OpenAI-compatible endpoint with per-team API keys
Rate limits and monthly budget caps
Model routing rules and automatic fallback on provider errors
Exact-match cache with TTL, plus an optional semantic cache with clear risks documented
PII redaction before logging
Request logs and a cost-per-team dashboard
Load test report
key_decisions: Where the cache key includes the tenant
How to count tokens for budgets before the call
Failover timing and idempotency
evaluation: Overhead the gateway adds at p95
Cache hit rate and cost saved on the replay
Failover time when a provider is down
Correctness of budget enforcement under concurrency
failure_modes_to_show: Cache serving stale or cross-tenant answers
Thundering herd after a provider outage
deliverables: Architecture diagram and a one-page threat model
talking_points: Routing and caching cut spend by X percent on replayed traffic.
I tested budget enforcement with 100 concurrent requests.

projects.name: Evaluation and regression CI for LLM apps
projects.pitch: A runner that executes your eval set on every pull request, compares model and prompt versions, and blocks changes that lower quality.
projects.why_it_stands_out: Almost nobody builds this, and every hiring manager wants it. Judge calibration against human labels is the detail that impresses.
corpus_ideas: Use the eval sets from your other projects
mvp: Versioned JSONL datasets
Runner that executes N samples per case for flaky outputs
Checks: exact match, schema validity, regex, LLM judge with a rubric
Judge calibration: agreement with 50 human labels
GitHub Action that posts a diff table as a pull request comment
Thresholds that fail the build
key_decisions: Which checks are code and which need a judge
How many samples per case
How you stop the judge from favoring longer or earlier answers
evaluation: Judge agreement with humans (and its disagreement cases)
Run time and cost per CI run
Flake rate on repeated runs
failure_modes_to_show: A prompt change that improves the average but breaks a critical case
deliverables: Repo plus a demo pull request showing a blocked regression
talking_points: A prompt tweak raised the average score but my critical-case check blocked it.
My judge agreed with humans on X of 50 labels.

projects.name: Repository-aware code assistant with test-based verification
projects.pitch: Ask where something is implemented or request a small change; the assistant retrieves relevant code, proposes a diff and runs the tests to check it.
projects.why_it_stands_out: It is the hardest retrieval problem (code) joined to the strongest verification signal (tests) and mirrors products people use daily.
mvp: Parse code into function and class chunks with a syntax-tree library
Symbol index with callers and callees
Hybrid retrieval over code and docs
Tool to apply a patch in a sandbox and run the test suite
Answers cite file paths and line ranges
Eval on 30 tasks: locate, explain, small fix
key_decisions: Chunk by symbol versus by file
How much of the call graph to include
What the agent may run and with which permissions
evaluation: Locate accuracy
Fix success rate with tests passing
Steps and cost per task
Unsafe command attempts blocked
failure_modes_to_show: Edits that pass tests but break behavior
deliverables: Write-up on what context mattered most
talking_points: Symbol-level chunking beat file-level chunking by X on locate accuracy.
Running the tests turned most hallucinated fixes into visible failures.
